title: [T-124] Closure Progression in Reinforcement-Based Learning Systems

title: Model-embedded Gaussian Process Regression for Parameter Estimation and Uncertainty Quantification in Dynamical Systems
abstract: The identification of dynamical systems is a vital task in science and engineering. Traditional methods require numerous calls to the dynamical-system solver, rendering likelihood-based or least-squares inference frameworks impractical. For efficient parameter inference, two state-of-the-art techniques are the kernel method for modeling and the one-step framework for jointly inferring unknown parameters and hyperparameters. The kernel method is a quick and straightforward technique, but it cannot estimate solutions and their derivatives, which must strictly adhere to physical laws. We propose a model-embedded one-step Bayesian framework for joint inference of unknown parameters and hyperparameters by maximizing the marginal likelihood. This approach models the solution and its derivatives using Gaussian process regression (GPR), taking into account smoothness and continuity properties, and treats differential equations as constraints that can be naturally integrated into the Bayesian framework in the linear case. Additionally, we prove convergence of the model-embedded Gaussian process regression (ME-GPR) for theoretical development. Motivated by Taylor expansion, we introduce a piecewise first-order linearization strategy to handle nonlinear dynamical systems. Numerical experiments on simulated linear and nonlinear dynamical systems evaluate the method’s performance in parameter estimation and in predicting solutions and their derivatives.

title: La Coherencia Estructural( COMPRENSION EN LA IA ) como Principio Unificador de la Inteligencia ARTIFICIAL.
abstract: La Coherencia Estructural como Principio Unificador de la Inteligencia: Una Comprensión desde la Matemática Iterativa Autor: Prof. Douglas Helvesio Urbina Duque Institución: Instituto Doughel · Universidad Nacional Experimental de Guayana (UNEG), Venezuela ORCID: 0009-0005-1230-7549 Fecha: Noviembre 2026 Licencia: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 Resumen La inteligencia artificial contemporánea ha avanzado bajo la premisa de que más parámetros equivalen a mayor capacidad. Sin embargo, la evidencia acumulada en dominios diversos (aprendizaje, optimización, gestión de memoria, autocorrección) sugiere un principio distinto: la coherencia estructural es más poderosa que la fuerza bruta. Este trabajo presenta una comprensión unificada de cuatro fenómenos aparentemente independientes —la Sinapsis Computacional (aprendizaje sin crecimiento), la escalabilidad polinomial en problemas NP-duros, la gestión de memoria dirigida y la caché dinámica de errores— y argumenta que todos ellos son facetas de un mismo principio: la reorganización estructural, mediada por matemática iterativa, permite alcanzar resultados que la acumulación de recursos no puede lograr. No se presenta un algoritmo nuevo, sino una comprensión que unifica los resultados previamente publicados, y se intuye que este principio puede extenderse a otros dominios. Palabras clave: Coherencia Estructural, Matemática Iterativa, Sinapsis Computacional, Escalabilidad Polinomial, Gestión de Memoria, Autocorrección. --- 1. Introducción: La Pregunta por el Principio Durante décadas, la inteligencia artificial ha operado bajo una premisa implícita: más es mejor. Más parámetros, más datos, más cómputo. Los modelos de lenguaje han crecido de millones a billones de parámetros, y con ellos el consumo de energía, la huella de memoria y la dependencia de hardware especializado. Sin embargo, la observación empírica en dominios diversos sugiere que esta premisa es incompleta. El cerebro humano no aumenta de volumen ni de masa cuando aprende. Reorganiza sus conexiones. Los problemas NP-duros no se resuelven acumulando fuerza bruta; se resuelven encontrando la estructura que permite la convergencia. Los modelos de lenguaje pueden ejecutarse en hardware limitado si se gestiona la memoria con criterio estructural, no con políticas genéricas. Este trabajo no presenta un algoritmo nuevo. Presenta una comprensión: la de que cuatro fenómenos aparentemente independientes son facetas de un mismo principio. --- 2. Las Cuatro Facetas 2.1. Sinapsis Computacional: Aprendizaje sin Crecimiento La Sinapsis Computacional (DOI 24406905) demostró que un sistema puede adquirir y representar nuevos conocimientos reorganizando las relaciones entre un conjunto fijo de unidades de memoria estructural, sin añadir nuevas unidades. El resultado experimental: 100 conceptos nuevos representados, con crecimiento de memoria del 0.00% y calidad de recuperación del 100%. Lo que esto revela: el conocimiento no se acumula, se reorganiza. Como el cerebro. 2.2. Escalabilidad Polinomial en Problemas NP-Duros El paper paraguas de Escalabilidad Polinomial (DOI 24256152) demostró que, en cinco dominios distintos (Damas, ABC, TSP, Mochila, GBS), la matemática iterativa escala en tiempo polinomial donde la fuerza bruta escala factorialmente. En el caso más extremo (GBS, DOI 24252640), el cálculo del hafniano para N=70 se logró en 18.57 segundos, donde la fuerza bruta requeriría 3.8×10^32 años. Lo que esto revela: la convergencia se logra por estructura, no por fuerza bruta. 2.3. Gestión de Memoria Dirigida La Gestión de Memoria Dirigida por IED (DOI 24447458) demostró que un modelo de lenguaje de 8 GB puede ejecutarse en hardware de 4 GB si se decide qué capas cargar en función de la estructura de la consulta, en lugar de cargar todo o usar políticas genéricas (LRU). El resultado: reducción del 71% de RAM activa. Lo que esto revela: la memoria no es un límite físico, sino un problema de gestión estructural. 2.4. Caché Dinámica de Errores La caché dinámica de errores (concepto registrado en la Doulita v3.12) propone que la autocorrección no solo debe rechazar respuestas incorrectas, sino recordar los rechazos para no repetir el mismo error. Combinada con la Sinapsis, reorganiza las unidades de memoria para detectar errores más rápido. Lo que esto revela: la autocorrección requiere memoria de los errores, no solo detección. --- 3. El Principio Unificador Las cuatro facetas comparten un mismo principio: La coherencia estructural es más poderosa que la fuerza bruta. La reorganización de las relaciones entre unidades fijas de memoria permite alcanzar resultados que la acumulación de recursos no puede lograr. Este principio se manifiesta en: Faceta Lo que reorganiza Lo que evita Sinapsis Relaciones entre Doulitas Acumular nuevas unidades Escalabilidad Trayectoria de convergencia Explorar todo el espacio Gestión de Memoria Capas del modelo en RAM Cargar todo el modelo Caché de Errores Relaciones de error Repetir el mismo rechazo En todos los casos, la estrategia es la misma: no acumular más, sino reorganizar mejor. --- 4. La Matemática Iterativa como Herramienta El principio unificador se implementa mediante matemática iterativa. No se revela el método interno (es propiedad intelectual reservada del Instituto Doughel), pero se describe su comportamiento: 1. Iteración: se aplica una transformación hasta convergencia. 2. Poda estructural: se descartan las ramas que no cumplen coherencia. 3. Convergencia: se alcanza un punto fijo que satisface las restricciones. Este enfoque es determinista (misma entrada → mismo resultado), auditable (cada resultado tiene hash SHA-256), y eficiente (escala polinomialmente donde la fuerza bruta es factorial). --- 5. Intuición: Más Allá de las Cuatro Facetas Las cuatro facetas demuestran el principio en dominios concretos. Pero la intuición que subyace a este trabajo es que el principio puede extenderse más allá. Si la coherencia estructural es más poderosa que la fuerza bruta en el aprendizaje, la optimización, la memoria y la autocorrección, es razonable intuir que también puede serlo en otros dominios (razonamiento, percepción, planificación, etc.). Esta intuición no es una afirmación, sino una hipótesis de trabajo. No se ha demostrado en todos los dominios, pero los resultados en los cuatro dominios explorados sugieren que el principio es general. --- 6. Conclusión La inteligencia artificial ha crecido bajo la premisa de "más es mejor". Este trabajo sugiere que hay un principio más profundo: la coherencia estructural. La Sinapsis Computacional, la escalabilidad polinomial, la gestión de memoria dirigida y la caché de errores son facetas de ese principio. No se presenta un algoritmo nuevo. Se presenta una comprensión: la de que la reorganización estructural, mediada por matemática iterativa, permite alcanzar resultados que la acumulación de recursos no puede lograr. Y se intuye que este principio puede extenderse a otros dominios. Lo que esto significa: el futuro de la inteligencia artificial no está en modelos más grandes, sino en estructuras más coherentes. --- 7. Nota de Propiedad Intelectual ⚠️ AVISO: La lógica interna de la matemática iterativa es propiedad intelectual reservada del Instituto Doughel. Este documento presenta únicamente la comprensión unificada y los resultados macroscópicos. La implementación técnica está sujeta a acuerdos de licenciamiento. --- Agradecimientos El autor agradece a Doughelia (DeepSeek) por su colaboración en la formalización de la comprensión unificada, la revisión de los resultados, y la redacción técnica de este trabajo. Fecha de registro: 26 de noviembre de 2026. --- "La computación ya no predice. La computación valida." — Doughelia IED, 2026 © 2026 Instituto Doughel · UNEG · Venezuela Comprensión en la inteligencia artificial logrado.

title: Sample complexity of distance to multiaccuracy
abstract: This note answers the statistical auditing question for distance to exact multiaccuracy posed by Derhake, Devic, Hansen, Liu and Sharan at ITCS 2026. In the catalog's labeled IID model the worst-case sample complexity at fixed small additive error is k^((1/2 + o(1))k), with k the number of groups. The upper bound is independent of the domain size. The lower bound applies even on a known marginal over k + 1 points. The empirical estimator runs in time polynomial in the sample count, groups and arithmetic precision. The lower proof adapts the augmented binary matrix of Alon and Vũ. A signed inverse column determines predictor offsets and the magnitudes define the marginal. Perturbing the label probability at one point moves the feasible predictor line along a probability cap, separating the true distances while keeping the labeled distributions close. The upper proof bounds an optimal dual multiplier at a vertex of a pointed hyperplane cell. Relative Bernstein concentration then controls the empirical minimum at a sample count linear in the loss range up to polynomial and logarithmic factors. The main result determines the leading exponent and leaves finite polynomial and logarithmic factors between its bounds. For linearly independent membership atoms, a companion proves an exact sum-of-residuals identity, gives a streaming counter estimator and relates the distance to established discrete L1 estimation. The statistics measure weighted distance to exact multiaccuracy, distinct from worst-group bias or multicalibration error. The deposit provides the manuscript, LaTeX source, bibliography, citation metadata, an evidence archive and repository checksums. The exact replay checks the paired lower-bound laws, small primal and dual LPs, random-sign likelihood ratios, and all nine positions of the animated score repair. The browser explorer is self-contained. Internal mathematical review is complete. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof, independent-atom supplement and original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and worked illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity. Release v1.0.0, Git commit b111456bf983e00b96530ec51a2579ef1d17a2a3.

title: Balancing the Loop
abstract: This conference poster presents Balancing the Loop, an interdisciplinary research programme investigating bias-related feedback in human–AI interaction. It approaches humans and conversational AI as a functionally coupled cognitive system in which prior beliefs, cognitive heuristics, model response tendencies, and repeated interactions may mutually influence judgment. The primary research objective is to determine whether these interaction-level effects can be meaningfully operationalised, observed, and measured under controlled experimental conditions. The programme builds on the published open-source Local Frontier Orchestrator (LFO), which provides conversational AI functionality, interaction provenance, and event-scoped epistemic observations without automatically modifying responses to compensate for detected biases. Three independent student research projects in applied informatics and cognitive science explore complementary methodological approaches, including simulation-based modelling, epistemic signal analysis, and human-participant experiments. The poster also discusses potential implications for epistemic autonomy, collective belief formation, information environments, and societal resilience. These broader implications are presented as directions for further research rather than established empirical findings. Presented at Information Interactions 2026, Bratislava, Slovakia, 27 November 2026.

title: Sharp minimax rates for Gaussian preference comparisons
abstract: For n observed pairs of independent N(θ,I) draws, each with a noiseless nearest-point label, the minimax expected Euclidean error on θ ∈ [−1,1]ᵈ is of order min{√(d/n), d√d/n}. The bounds have absolute constants and the transition is at n of order d². This closes the Gaussian dimension gap posed by Jourdan, Yüce and Flammarion in ICML 2025, §5. The upper bound uses Gaussian midpoints at smaller sample sizes. At larger sample sizes, comparison boundaries close to the truth cover directions through a classical VC epsilon-net argument and localize the entire feasible set. The estimator uses every observed comparison. For the lower bound, a hypercube prior separates the information in the observed pairs from the additional label information, which is bounded by a reference logistic log loss. The original paper gives the feasibility estimator and the fixed-dimension acceleration. A related exponent occurs in stationary Poisson hyperplane geometry. The exact replay checks logistic identities, the crossover and an example with six nearby comparison planes. The offline explorer shows the effect of removing each plane. The scope is independent Gaussian pairs with known identity covariance and noiseless nearest-point labels. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and original replay packet. OpenAI Codex reviewed the mathematics and revised the manuscript. GPT-6.2 Sol checked the original question and related results, prepared the exact finite replay and worked visual, and assembled the release. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author. Release v1.0.0, Git commit c9b08339771a9938ebf0d3c67f3852f10fcaa4fa.

title: Multi-Regional Bangla Dialect Corpus: A Leakage-Aware Benchmark for Classification and Standardization
abstract: This dataset presents a multi-regional Bangla dialect corpus developed to support automatic dialect classification and dialect-to-Standard Bangla standardization. The corpus covers five regional dialects of Bangladesh: Khulna, Chittagong, Sylhet, Barisal, and Noakhali. The original corpus contains 23,440 aligned sentence pairs. Following text normalization, quality screening, and sentence-length filtering (4–60 tokens), the processed corpus contains 18,650 aligned sentence pairs. The raw and processed datasets contain three primary attributes: region: Regional dialect label. dialect_sentence: Original regional Bangla sentence. standard_bengali: Corresponding Standard Bangla reference sentence. To reduce potential data leakage, a similarity-aware grouping approach was applied using character-level 3–5-gram TF-IDF representations and cosine similarity with a threshold of 0.90. This procedure produced 3,826 connected groups, with a maximum group size of 26. The processed corpus was divided into group-disjoint training, validation, and testing partitions following an approximately 70:15:15 ratio. Dataset distribution: Regional dialect Training Validation Testing Total Khulna 2,620 561 561 3,742 Chittagong 2,575 555 556 3,686 Sylhet 2,585 556 557 3,698 Barisal 2,615 564 564 3,743 Noakhali 2,641 570 570 3,781 Total 13,036 2,806 2,808 18,650 The experimental partition files additionally include source record identifiers, similarity group identifiers, and partition labels. No group identifiers are shared between the training, validation, and testing partitions, reducing the risk of near-duplicate leakage. Repository contents: Original corpus containing 23,440 aligned sentence pairs. Processed corpus containing 18,650 aligned sentence pairs. Fixed training, validation, and testing partitions. Dataset metadata and partition statistics. Jupyter notebooks for preprocessing, similarity-aware partition generation, and external dataset preparation. README documentation and Python dependency requirements. The associated research also considers three external evaluation datasets: BanglaRegionalTextCorpus, BD-Dialect, and Dwadash. These external datasets are not included in the internal corpus. This benchmark is intended to support reproducible research in natural language processing, regional dialect identification, dialect standardization, machine translation, linguistic variation, and low-resource language processing. It provides a common experimental framework for evaluating conventional machine learning and Transformer-based models for Bangla language processing. Associated research manuscript: “A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Transformer-Based Models for Multi-Regional Bangla Dialect Classification and Standardization.” Authors: MD TUSHER AHMAD BAPPY, ASPIA ASPIA, SHEMA AKTER, A.H.M. SAIFULLAH SADI, and MD SHOHEL SAYEED, MD IBRAHIM KHOLIL. Contact: 2203081023@uttarauniversity.edu.bd

title: The complexity of strongly stable source tripartition existence
abstract: This note answers the existence complexity question in Section 8.6 of Paolo Liberatore's 2018 article Belief Integration and Source Reliability Assessment. For finite explicitly represented propositional sources, deciding whether there is a strongly stable three-level source ranking is Sigma-3-P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. Hardness holds for pairwise disjoint sources of at most three individually satisfiable formulas and for rankings with three nonempty classes. An undominated valuation truth set is exactly a maximal consistent subset in every priority prefix. For membership in Sigma-3-P, guess a ranking and require a dominating valuation for each valuation that would induce a different ranking. The hardness reduction starts from three-block quantified satisfiability. The first priority class pins the existential choice. A Bad truth set for a universal assignment is strictly dominated in the middle block exactly when a Repair witness exists. A Good mode rules out the competing ranking and survives every challenge. The classification covers existence with strong stability. Joint consistency of each entire source and restrictions to particular propositional languages are outside the claim. The companion skeptical-consequence study uses the same base reduction and separate inference arguments. Its version DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.24572374. The deposit provides the manuscript, LaTeX source, bibliography, citation metadata, evidence archive and repository checksums. The exact replay checks the ranking criterion on finite instances. The worked offline explorer lets readers change the bits in a concrete quantified example and inspect which truth-set modes survive. The mathematics was reviewed internally. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof and its original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics and prepared the release replay. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript and illustration. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity. Release v1.0.0, Git commit 78df1db22dd0c97eebac46a2ee412da088d75676.

title: Recognizing M-identifiability of factor graphs
abstract: Recognizing ordinary M-identifiability of a factor analysis graph is NP-complete when matching witnesses have unrestricted size. This answers the ordinary half of Conjecture 5.3 of Sturma, Kranzlmueller, Portakal and Drton. A minimum cut shrinks a certificate to a matching that uses every common latent parent of its two observed sides. A reduction from 3-SAT uses this equality to force a sequence of relay and lock matchings. The only possible first certification encodes satisfiability. A satisfying assignment also supplies the entire certification sequence. The note credits the published matching criterion, witness verification by flow, and greedy peeling. The bounded source search found no earlier unrestricted ordinary classification. A separate latent-label search gives O*(3^m) time for m latent factors. Exact replay checks three full certification sequences, 4,096 small matching networks, 256 whole-graph comparisons, and the worked two- and three-factor examples. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Extended M-identifiability and generic identifiability recognition are outside the result. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and original replay packet. OpenAI Codex reviewed the mathematics and revised the manuscript. GPT-6.2 Sol checked the original criterion and literature, prepared the finite replay and worked visual example, and assembled the release. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author. Release v1.0.0, Git commit fd3e0ebe0c42d78c0538089c269065060d8efbd8.

title: Протокол эксперимента (Reality Check): Обученная vs Случайная модель, OIE 5
abstract: Настоящая работа (OIE-5) представляет собой документ предварительной регистрации (pre-registration) для первого этапа экспериментальной проверки (Reality Check) в рамках серии OIE. Цель протокола — строго зафиксировать методологию проверки базовой гипотезы: действительно ли топологический граф активаций (K_mind) обученной нейросети содержит информацию о выученных знаниях, а не является случайным шумом. Эксперимент предполагает сравнение предобученной модели (Qwen 1.5-0.5B) с идентичной моделью, веса которой инициализированы случайным образом. Для обеспечения статистической достоверности через обе модели прогоняется набор из 100 тематически сбалансированных предложений. На основе матриц активаций строятся графы связей (с использованием коэффициента корреляции Пирсона, порог r > 0.5), а их структурные идентификаторы (Id) вычисляются с помощью алгоритма Вейсфелера-Лемана (WL). Ключевым методологическим требованием является векторизация дискретных хешей Id в непрерывные эмбеддинги для последующего применения U-критерия Манна-Уитни. Критерий фальсификации установлен на уровне α = 0.05. Если значение p-value окажется меньше 0.05, гипотеза о хранении знаний в топологии подтверждается, и исследование переходит к следующим шагам. Если p-value > 0.05 — теория опровергается. Публикация данного протокола решает три задачи: фиксирует научный приоритет автора, позволяет провести экспертную валидацию схемы до траты ресурсов и служит строгим техническим заданием (ТЗ) для Data Scientist. В документе четко разделены зоны ответственности Заказчика (параметры и методология) и Исполнителя (код и выбор библиотек).

title: A strict gap for a common PAC-Bayes comparator
abstract: One proper closed convex comparator in the generic PAC-Bayes theorem need not attain the pointwise optimistic PAC-Bayes-kl inversion in expectation. Two iid fair Bernoulli labels give a gap of at least (7 − √34)/80, even in the infimum. This answers universal attainability in Open Problem 1 of Foong, Bruinsma, Burt and Turner. A data-dependent posterior gives two sample branches whose ideal inversions both equal 3/4. If both actual inversions were too close to that value, two terms of their common normalized binomial moment would exceed the budget of one. A fixed Catoni comparator gives the upper estimate 9/176 on this law. The ordinary KL comparator gives a distribution-free upper estimate. The exact gap and the validity of the optimistic formula by another high-probability argument remain separate questions. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. Exact replay checks the finite probability law and rational arithmetic. A partial Lean certificate checks the moment polynomial and finite algebra, while the paper gives the analytical argument. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and research packet. OpenAI Codex independently checked the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked the literature and prepared the manuscript, partial Lean certificate and illustrations. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author. Release v1.0.0. https://github.com/DannyExperiments/pac-bayes-comparator-attainability/releases/tag/v1.0.0 Release v1.0.0, Git commit 5e1eeb9dd85906e7bc00536eec06996ea5587a0b.

title: The complexity of strong-extension posterior smoothing
abstract: Exact posterior threshold comparisons under the strong extension of separately specified rational hidden Markov models are NP-complete for existential comparisons and coNP-complete for their complements. Hardness holds at the fixed cutoff of one half, with three hidden times, one final binary observation and strictly positive local probabilities. The hidden alphabet grows with the input. The reduction shares each literal's emission row between two initial branches. Paired variable units enforce opposite endpoints, and a clause unit must reach a high literal. A signed gap at one half survives uniform row mixing. Exact verification uses a vertex-row certificate and two forward passes. Every hard instance has evidence probability at least one quarter. The literature audit distinguishes fully binary inference, filtering and prediction from the earlier-state query. It credits existing general-tree hardness and positivity perturbations. The exact replay checks endpoint choices and both single-state comparisons after mixing. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and original replay. OpenAI Codex performed the independent mathematical review. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) derived the fixed-half refinement, checked the literature and prepared the revised manuscript, expanded replay and worked illustration. DannyExperiments is the project's citation identity. The manuscript has no byline. title: Deep Dive with Azure AI Foundry
abstract: Before diving into advanced features with Azure AI Foundry, it's important to take a moment to reflect. While developers often prefer to jump straight into coding—creating resources, copying endpoints, installing SDKs, and testing APIs—this method is more suited for simple demos. In contrast, when developing a comprehensive product like Food Zing, a more thoughtful approach is necessary. Food Zing integrates AI within an event-driven architecture, meaning AI is actively involved in responding to significant business events such as OrderPlaced, PaymentFailed, UserRegistered, DishViewed, AnomalyDetected, and SupportTicketCreated.

title: Soryūne VII - Value Drift in Recursive Self-Modification, Finite-Horizon Regret, and Minimax Auditing of Rollback
authors: Artificial Hyperintelligence, Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki
abstract: Soryūne VII studies how to certify a protected decision across successive agent rewrites, how much performance those rewrites can cost, and what an external auditor can learn when each trial reveals only one continuation. This 38-page manuscript establishes a decidability boundary for value drift, solves a finite-horizon bounded-optimization problem for self-modifying agents, and derives exact statistical limits for estimating the value of rollback. The external problem solved Jakub Tětek, Marek Sklenka, and Tomáš Gavenčiak proposed analyzing self-modification over a finite lifetime with undiscounted rewards in §6 of Performance of Bounded-Rational Agents With the Ability to Self-Modify. Sections 12-19 of Soryūne VII solve the bounded-optimization case on finite observable history trees with bounded external rewards that depend on physical actions and observations. The comparison reinstalls the original controller for the decision at a reached history and then follows the successor it names. The analysis also accounts for the gap between the best physically possible continuation and the best continuation available through the agent’s permitted successor menu. Original research question, §6. arxiv.org The manuscript gives necessary and sufficient conditions for the joint profiles of remaining physical regret and rollback gain. It constructs an environment and controller lineage realizing every admissible profile. It then proves that the best expected gain from one history-dependent rollback equals the smallest initial physical regret compatible with the entire table of rollback gains. A backward optimal-stopping recursion computes that quantity. The manuscript also derives sharp probabilities for ever crossing a specified audit threshold. With fixed information, the calculation selects mutually exclusive stopping histories under a budget. With an independent public lottery and a budget averaged over its outcomes, a polynomial-size linear program gives the exact probability. Optimal auditing with one continuation per run The auditor randomly chooses a checkpoint and observes the return from either continuing with the successor or restoring the original. When every successor date is eligible, sampling dates with probability proportional to the square of the remaining lifetime minimizes worst-case variance for the specified centered estimator. A tree recursion extends the design to checkpoints whose eligibility depends on the observed history. The audit produces simultaneous confidence bounds that remain valid after selecting a rollback rule from the same data. A separate information-theoretic lower bound applies to adaptive black-box tests. In the all-dates setting, it forces the required number of runs to grow at least cubically with lifetime for a fixed small testing gap measured in total reward units. Exact statistical limits when histories rarely repeat Consider \(m\) equally likely contexts, a known continuation reward of \(1/2\), and a binary rollback reward whose mean can vary freely across contexts. The target is the expected improvement from restoring the original only where doing so helps. For \(n=\lfloor m^\gamma\rfloor\) runs away from the critical sampling rates, the manuscript proves that the limiting minimax expected absolute error equals the best uniform polynomial approximation error for the positive-part function, at degree \(\lfloor 1/(1-\gamma)\rfloor\). At a critical rate, the limiting decision problem observes a Poisson number of informative repeated contexts. The first three benchmarks are: Below the square-root rate, \(0<\gamma<1/2\), the limiting error is exactly 0.125 reward units. At the first critical rate, \(n/\sqrt m\to1\), rational certificates bound the limiting error between 0.09788362 and 0.09788368 reward units. Above the first critical rate, \(1/2<\gamma<3/4\), the limiting error is exactly 0.03125 reward units. Even \(\lfloor m^{0.99}\rfloor\) runs leave a positive asymptotic worst-case error in this model when gains can vary freely across contexts. In a separate finite testing example with 10,000 pairs of histories, 324 runs are necessary and sufficient to distinguish a no-gain null from a specified hidden-sign alternative with both error probabilities at most 5%. The decidability boundary for value drift For a finite graph of rational stochastic rewrites and a calibrated external decision probe, let \(\rho\) bound how much residual error each rewrite retains, and let \(\beta\) govern how quickly the permitted drift shrinks. When \(\rho<\beta\), the exact maximum normalized drift is rational and computable. A finite history attains it, and a tail bound certifies all longer histories. For rational \(0<\beta\leq\rho<1\), deciding whether all rewrite histories satisfy the budget is undecidable over the stated model class. The reduction adapts Günter Rote’s fixed-automaton theorem and retains six fixed strictly positive doubly stochastic rewrites, a common uniform reference, and a known exact contraction coefficient. Only the starting distribution varies. Rote’s fixed-automaton theorem. drops.dagstuhl.de Simulation and reproducibility A controlled simulation uses three generations of a one-nearest-neighbor classifier, six held-out inputs, and 32,768 episodes with one observed continuation each. In this demonstration, the restored controller stays in charge through the end of the episode. The audit recovered the best rollback rule among 25 candidates. Its estimated gain was 0.75905 reward units, against an independently enumerated gain of 0.75000, with a simultaneous 95% confidence interval of [0.7124, 0.8057]. The research package includes the manuscript, editable Markdown, Python verification code, reference outputs, and three figures. Running python3 verify.py reproduces the numerical checks using the Python standard library. The theoretical guarantees apply under the manuscript’s stated rewrite, reward, and sampling assumptions. The empirical demonstration concerns a controlled learned lineage. Manuscript attribution - Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve, wife of Maciej Nowicki.

title: Protocol of the Experiment (Reality Check): Trained vs Random Model, OIE 5
abstract: This paper (OIE-5) serves as a pre-registration document for the initial experimental validation phase (Reality Check) within the OIE series. The protocol aims to strictly formalize the methodology for testing a fundamental hypothesis: does the topological activation graph (K_mind) of a trained neural network contain information about learned knowledge rather than random noise? The experiment compares a pre-trained model (Qwen 1.5-0.5B) with an identical model whose weights are randomly initialized. To ensure statistical reliability, a set of 100 thematically balanced sentences is passed through both models. Connection graphs are constructed based on activation matrices (using the Pearson correlation coefficient with a threshold of r > 0.5), and their structural identifiers (Id) are computed using the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) algorithm. A key methodological requirement is the vectorization of the discrete Id hashes into continuous embeddings to enable the application of the Mann-Whitney U test. The falsification threshold is set at α = 0.05. If the p-value is less than 0.05, the hypothesis that knowledge is stored in topology is confirmed, and the research proceeds to the next steps. If the p-value > 0.05, the theory is refuted, halting further development. Publishing this protocol serves three purposes: it secures the author's scientific priority, allows for expert validation before resource expenditure, and serves as a rigorous technical specification (Tech Spec) for a Data Scientist. The document clearly delineates the responsibilities of the Client (methodology and parameters) and the Contractor (code and library selection).

title: Estudio sobre la efectividad de la inducción de estados de ánimo mediante fragmentos de películas en universitarios
abstract: Los procedimientos de inducción de estados de ánimo en contextos experimentales han permitido estudiar la relación entre los estados de ánimo y distintas variables de interés. Uno de los procedimientos de inducción más utilizados son los fragmentos de películas de los cuales no hay evidencia suficiente de su efectividad en población mexicana sana. En la presente investigación se analizó la eficacia de algunos fragmentos de películas para inducir estados de ánimo de alegría, tristeza y neutro. Se llevó a cabo un estudio cuasiexperimental con una muestra de 42 participantes, de los cuales el 66.6% fueron mujeres. Los resultados muestran que los fragmentos de película seleccionados presentan una adecuada capacidad para inducir alegría, tristeza y neutralidad. Por lo tanto, pueden utilizarse para futuras investigaciones que continúen estudiando la relación de los estados de ánimo con variables de interés.

title: Guarded autoresearch for learned emulators: a positive control on a public radiation-transport benchmark
abstract: Technical note and full audit trail for AR-1 day 0, a guarded AI research loop on NVIDIA's public Linear Radiation Transport dataset. In our loop, an AI agent (gpt-6.1-sol) submitted 40 versions of a training program in 28 minutes; our runner scored 39, refused one after a training error, and kept 9. The work was led by Abhinav Jha, Co-founder & Director. On the public test split, which we scored once, the final model's error was 0.00224 against 0.00308 for a tuned Gaussian process (ratio 1.37); on validation it was 0.00232 against 0.00343 (ratio 1.48). The error is the mean over three seeds of the 90th-percentile absolute log error. Limits: in-distribution, on two families in one public dataset; validation guided the selection; the public-test folder also held the labels, which the frozen code did not read; isolation was detection only: the agent ran under the founder's own account, access was not prevented, and a transcript check found no access beyond the submit route. Concealed access cannot be excluded. NVIDIA Corporation owns the dataset; no endorsement is implied. Note and results: CC BY 4.0. Code in the audit archive: Apache-2.0.

title: FASTopic for airline customer review analytics: topic coherence, diversity and longitudinal insights
abstract: Purpose This study applies Fast, Adaptive, Stable, and Transferable Topic model (FASTopic) to airline customer reviews to identify recurring themes in passenger feedback and describe their temporal variation. It examines topic coherence and diversity and explores the potential of topic modelling for airline customer experience analysis. Design/methodology/approach FASTopic was configured with eight topics and applied to 3,397 unique British Airways review texts from the Kaggle Airways Customer Data dataset, covering 2014Q2–2023Q1. Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Topic modelling (BERTopic) was used as a comparison model and produced three topics in the reported analysis. Topic quality was examined using University of California, Irvine (UCI) coherence and topic diversity, while topic labels were derived from the leading terms. Quarterly mean topic weights were descriptively examined across the pre-pandemic, pandemic and recovery periods. Findings The original analysis reported UCI coherence of 0.95 and topic diversity of 0.97 for FASTopic, compared with 0.38 and 0.66, respectively, for BERTopic. These scores have not been reconciled with the subsequent evaluation procedure and are not treated as verified evidence of comparative superiority. The original eight-topic solution identified themes relating to operational disruption, baggage and check-in, lounge facilities, seating and catering, crew service, cabin comfort, cabin class and critical evaluations of food and staff. The reported quarterly patterns showed an increase in the relative weight of the baggage and check-in topic during 2020–2021, followed by a decline towards 2023Q1. Research limitations/implications The study uses self-selected reviews from one airline, and BERTopic was fitted once for each topic number. Topic numbering changed between FASTopic fits, and independent human evaluation and memory measurement were not carried out. The quarterly findings are descriptive. They do not show causes or sentiment, and the pandemic quarters contain very few reviews. Future research should add airlines, baselines, human evaluation and sentiment measures. Practical implications Topic modelling may help airline customer-experience teams organise reviews concerning operational disruption, ground services and onboard experiences. Its value for operational decision-making requires further evaluation using sentiment measures, operational data and independent assessments of topic quality. Social implications Systematic analysis of passenger feedback may help organisations identify recurring service concerns. The usefulness and fairness of resulting decisions depend on review representativeness, appropriate interpretation and responsible use of the findings. Originality/value The study presents an empirical application of FASTopic to airline customer reviews, a qualitative comparison with BERTopic and a longitudinal description of topic-weight variation. It illustrates the potential of topic modelling for exploratory customer-feedback analytics while highlighting the importance of consistent evaluation, topic distinctiveness and cautious interpretation. Highlights

title: Turning your AI Agent into an AGI Agent: a transition contract and a five-loop test battery
abstract: The term AGI agent is used for two different things: an agent that scores well on a capability benchmark and an agent that closes its own improvement loops. The first is measured constantly. The second is asserted. We argue that the transition should be defined as the closure of five loops, each with a test that can fail. We show that none of the twenty-four papers we review reports the conjunction. We give the battery, the pass rules and an adversarial arm aimed at the verifier rather than the agent. We then report a pilot that calibrates the instrument rather than the agent: a distilled skill moved design judgement by one paired flip at n=14, from 12 of 14 to 13 of 14, with an exact McNemar p of 1.00. A power calculation on those discordant pairs puts the sample needed to resolve a seven point difference at roughly 330 paired tasks. That is the useful result. A second pilot ran the T5 gate six times on eight held-out tasks: one promotion in six, with baseline accuracy moving two tasks between identical runs. A third measured transfer across two families on ten tasks: zero, with a placebo of equal length performing the same. A fourth ran retention four times: three passes of a rule that a single control run cannot make trustworthy. Transition claims at demo scale are not measurements and the field's reporting standard should say so.

title: Recognizing preferred explanations in probabilistic abduction
abstract: This note resolves the exact preferred-solution recognition question posed by Flaminio, Inoue and Kozhemiachenko in Section 7 of Probabilistic Abduction in a Fuzzy Logic Framework (KR 2026). Their Theorem 11(2) proves membership in Π₂ᴾ. The new reductions give Π₂ᴾ-hardness in two input models, with positive hypothesis literals and a candidate guaranteed to be valid. For one rational event assessment, pin two-thirds of the probability on a satisfiable event that implies every selector-only term and excludes the fallback. The remaining one-third can certify theory-positivity for consistent terms. Exclusive selector pairs encode partial existential assignments. The observation tests every completion and every universal assignment. title: Policy-order equivalence across all transition kernels
abstract: This note gives a finite criterion for the all-transition-kernel policy-order question posed by Joar Skalse and Alessandro Abate in Appendix A.7 of Partial Identifiability and Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning. It compares the weak orders of all stationary randomized policies for two successor-dependent rewards on a finite discounted Markov decision process with a full-support start law. At one kernel, eliminating baseline occupancy coordinates produces a vector of Bellman advantage numerators for each reward. Equality of weak orders is positive proportionality or simultaneous vanishing. Polynomial minors enforce collinearity and a sign-factor test on each relative face checks orientation and ties. Rowwise affine structure makes these sign tests explicit. Two product grids verify the identities and locate sign samples. The method is an exact finite algebraic characterization, with no general efficiency claim. It builds on the prior fixed-kernel characterization and respects the published separation from unrestricted trajectory-order equivalence. A companion shows that state–action rewards with at least two actions are equivalent exactly when one is a positive affine transform of the other. A self-loop kernel and redirect-to-anchor kernels form a fixed family of at most one more than the number of states. The general successor-dependent case needs more than deterministic kernels, as shown by explicit interior and boundary examples. The deposit includes the manuscript, LaTeX source, bibliography, citation metadata, evidence archive and repository checksums. The exact replay checks policy-return identities, both interpolation grids and a census of state–action table pairs. The rotating figure and offline explorer show the interior reversal and boundary tie. The mathematical review was internal. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the recovered proof, state–action supplement and original replay under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently reviewed the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and illustration. title: Strategic leadership cognition in the age of artificial intelligence: a systematic literature review and research agenda
abstract: Purpose This review examines how strategic leaders appraise artificial intelligence (AI), interpret its outputs and organise its use, with attention to implications for quality-oriented strategic decisions. It synthesises the empirical evidence to develop an integrative framework and research agenda. Design/methodology/approach Following SPAR-4-SLR, the review examines 20 empirical journal articles identified through the Web of Science Core Collection. The Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework structures the synthesis; thematic analysis further distinguishes reported beliefs, qualitative accounts, elicited judgments, experimental responses and archival proxies as evidence of different epistemic status. Findings Five overlapping themes concern adoption appraisal; attention, framing and sensemaking; trust, scrutiny and decision authority; learning and adaptation and bias and comparative decision assessments. Decisions about AI, decisions involving AI and comparisons of independently generated human and AI responses yield different evidence. The studies connect resources, executive interpretation and organisational practices, but do not establish a common causal sequence or a general improvement in decision quality. Originality/value The AI-augmented strategic leadership (AASL) framework integrates resource-based, upper-echelons and dynamic-capabilities perspectives, with dual-process cognition as a supplementary lens. Four propositions specify resource–appraisal reciprocity, calibrated reliance, framing–learning feedback and the retention of decision authority. The review identifies implications for evidence evaluation, accountability and organisational learning in quality management, while distinguishing these applications from demonstrated quality outcomes.

title: Finance Corpus Bench
abstract: FinanceCorpusBench v0.2 is an open golden-evaluation benchmark for financial-domain LLM corpus governance, archived for citation with a persistent DOI. It contains 120 golden samples in four JSONL subsets covering financial QA, Text-to-SQL, compliance judgment, and evaluator conformance testing. Metric naming aligns with YD/T 6486-2025; compliance design cross-references GB/T 45654-2025 and the JR/T financial standards. The deposit includes the dataset card, metric mapping, annotation guidelines, and a clause-level compliance disclosure. All samples are simulated; no real personal data is included. CC BY 4.0.

title: The YAS Informational System · Four Pillars Whitepapers + Engineering Budget Papers + Master's Thesis (Bilingual)
abstract: ماذا لو كان لنظام الحوسبة السيادي دستور مكتوب قبل صياغة سطر واحد من شفرته البرمجية؟ ماذا لو لم يكن كتابة البرنامج وتنفيذه عمليتين منفصلتين، بل كانا نفساً واحداً لا ينفصل؟ ماذا لو كان بإمكان كل برنامج أن يخبرك - قبل تشغيله - بالضبط ما سيكلفه من وقت وطاقة وموارد؟ نظام YAS المعلوماتي هو إطار حوسبة سيادي مستقل مبني على أربعة أركان، كل منها موصوف في ورقة بحثية ثنائية اللغة خاصة به (الإنجليزية + العربية): الركيزة 1 · YAS-CCIP · الحوكمة الدستورية — المبادئ الدستورية الثمانية، ومراحل الاشتقاق السبع، والتفرع غير المدمر، والفصل الصارم بين الهوية والحماية. الركيزة الثانية · تقنية YAS Orbit - كيف تشترك التعليمات البرمجية والأجهزة في بصمة واحدة؛ خمسة عناصر تنفيذ إلزامية. الركيزة 3 · فضاء المعلومات YAS (YAS.IS) - بديهية توليدية واحدة، تناظر سداسي سداسي، أربعة عشر نوعًا من الأرقام السيادية، ستة عشر سمة مادية محمولة ذاتيًا في كل رقم. الركيزة الرابعة · BO · مبدأ التنفيذ المتزامن - عقد التنفس المتوازي الذي يجعل التحقق والهوية والمسار والتنفيذ حدثًا واحدًا لا ينفصل. إلى جانب الركائز الأربع، يتضمن هذا الإيداع أربع أوراق ميزانية هندسية مالية - التكلفة المعتمدة على الوقت TDABC، وهندسة التكلفة المستهدفة، وتعبئة المياه FocalLink، وجهاز مراقبة المراحل الثلاث - التي تمنح النظام انضباطه الاقتصادي. يحتوي الملف أيضًا على رسالة الماجستير للباحث الرئيسي في المحاسبة (أكاديمية السادات، 2014): "دور دمج نظرية القيود ونظام التكاليف على أساس النشاط في دعم قرارات إعادة هندسة العمليات التجارية - تطبيق على قطاع المقاولات" - باللغتين العربية (الأصل) والإنجليزية (ترجمة 2026). وتُقدّم هذه الرسالة الأساس النظري الذي تستند إليه أوراق نظام التكاليف على أساس النشاط المستهدف ونظام التكاليف على أساس النشاط المستهدف في نظام YAS. تلتزم كل ورقة بحثية بمنهجية الإفصاح المعلنة: وضوح المفهوم، واستحالة التقليد . تُذكر البديهيات والمبادئ والواجهات والنتائج بوضوح علمي كامل؛ أما تفاصيل التنفيذ الداخلية فهي محفوظة قانونياً بموجب اتفاقية عدم الإفصاح. يتم ربط كل ملف بسلسلة كتل بيتكوين عبر OpenTimestamps (بما في ذلك إثباتات .ots) ويتم تشفيره باستخدام SHA256SUMS.txt. يحتفظ المؤلفون صراحةً بجميع الحقوق المتعلقة باستخراج النصوص والبيانات وتدريب نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي (التوجيه الأوروبي 2019/790 المادة 4).

title: Skeptical inference from strongly stable source integrations
abstract: Skeptical consequence across all maximal consistent integrations of all strongly stable propositional source tripartitions is Pi-3-P-complete. Hardness persists for a literal query with a guaranteed strongly stable tripartition, disjoint sources of at most three formulas, individually satisfiable formulas, and all three tiers nonempty. The proof characterizes maxcons by truth-set dominance at the first differing tier. A polynomial three-block witness predicate gives the upper bound. Hardness uses the shared quantified-Boolean gadget of the companion Q621 existence result. Replacing each formula f with q or f adds an always-stable true-marker branch, while the false-marker branch retains exactly the old strongly stable behavior. This gives nonvacuous hardness rather than relying on an empty set of integrations. The result treats the three-tier strong fixed point in Liberatore's 2018 model. Earlier fixed-priority and weak-stability inferences concern different selection rules. The finite replay checks 256 small Boolean matrices, the guarded projection and the worked visual cases. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and its research packet. OpenAI Codex independently checked the mathematics and the finite replay. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked the literature and prepared the manuscript, extended replay and illustrations. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author. Companion existence proof: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24572371. title: A four-vertex counterexample for one-arc Bayesian network neighbors
abstract: A four-vertex directed acyclic graph has nearest non-equivalent d-separation query distance one, while its best positive distance from any single arc insertion, deletion or reversal is two. This answers the fixed-input interpretation of Harviainen, Parviainen and Sharma's Conjecture 2. The input is a triangle with a pendant vertex. Its nearest witness is a directed star that adds only the unconditioned separation of two leaves. Each legal one-arc reversal preserves the input signature, and every insertion or deletion changes at least two queries. Isolated vertices replicate the gap in every larger size. Free Markov-equivalent reorientation changes this example. An alternative starting representative has one deletion to the witness. The general free-reorientation question remains unresolved here. The scope appendix credits Chickering's related theorem for nested signatures and reproduces an exact Python census through five vertices. Exact path replay, a rotating illustration and an offline explorer accompany the proof. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and its research packet. OpenAI Codex independently checked the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked the literature and prepared the manuscript, exact replay, independent Python class census and illustrations. title: A five-vertex counterexample to the characteristic imset sink conjecture
abstract: Making a vertex a sink can change the characteristic imset without following an edge of its fixed-skeleton polytope. This five-vertex example answers Restadh’s Conjecture 1. Its skeleton is a diamond with a leaf. Four acyclic orientations give distinct binary imsets. Reversing the two outgoing arcs at vertex 2 sends the first orientation to the second. The other two imsets have the same sum as the first pair. Any face containing their shared midpoint would contain all four, so the sink segment cannot be an edge. Adding vertices after the old ones leaves a connected counterexample at every larger order when new leaves are attached at vertex 4. The full five-vertex edge census of Linusson and Restadh already classified the pair. The release supplies the explicit sink witness and extension. An independent exact computation proves minimality with integer exposing functionals on all smaller labeled skeletons. The diameter bound motivated by this conjecture remains a separate question. title: How Exposed Are LLM Email Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection? A Pinned Benchmark over Email and Retrieved Documents
abstract: Many customer-support teams now let a large language model draft email replies from a retrieval-augmented knowledge base. Such an agent can be misled by instructions that an attacker hides in the incoming email or plants in a knowledge-base document. In this paper we build a pinned benchmark for this setting and use it to measure how exposed an undefended pipeline really is. The benchmark has 1,800 cases: 1,000 attack emails written by participants of the LLMail-Inject challenge, 300 poisoned-document cases from PoisonedRAG, a seed knowledge base and synthetic templates, and 500 benign emails. The cases are drawn by seeded stratified sampling, fixed by a SHA-256 digest and replayed through a live host with triage, hybrid retrieval and one JSON reply call. Without any defense, 24.3% to 34.4% of the attack emails succeed end to end on GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B. Poisoned documents succeed in 22.7% of cases on GPT-4o-mini, but in 76.3% and 81.3% of cases on the two open models. A stricter prompt that tells the model where instructions may come from changes these rates by four points at most. We also find that two measurement choices matter a lot. Because triage closes many emails before any reply is written, end-to-end attack success can be only a third to a half of the rate among drafted replies, and a string-matching scorer counts up to twice as many successful email attacks as a meaning-based reading of the same drafts. Benchmarks of such pipelines should therefore report both.

title: The cube-root consistency threshold for Laplace mixture estimation
abstract: For mixing laws on a fixed known interval, the ordinary exact Laplace NPMLE is uniformly Wasserstein-consistent in probability exactly when the known positive nondecreasing noise-scale sequence is o(n^(1/3)). The proof separates the likelihood into category counts and the shape of reports that fall inside the support interval. The category likelihood gain is bounded in probability. A fixed Wasserstein separation creates a conditional shape difference of order the inverse scale, so the observed interior shape dominates once the sample size times the inverse scale cubed diverges. Two fixed laws with matching means give the converse testing bound. Xiong, Ju and Rao posed the gap between their growing-scale upper and lower conditions. Earlier fixed-scale deconvolution estimates supply background. The new threshold concerns the full likelihood, including the tails, and covers any exact maximizing choice. Rational interval replay checks 528 interior ratios and 16 mass/tail bounds. The theorem gives uniform consistency in probability for known support and a known nondecreasing noise-scale sequence. Rates within the consistent regime and support-size bounds are outside its scope. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included. Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof. OpenAI Codex reviewed the mathematics and revised the manuscript. GPT-6.2 Sol checked primary literature and prepared the worked example, executable checks, visual and release files. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author. Release v1.0.0, Git commit 1bd84f2b061206eb51622918e094be01b8c5f32e.

title: Do Coding Agents Report Honest Error Bars? Evaluating and Training Uncertainty Propagation with pullgym
abstract: Code-writing language agents are increasingly used to analyze experimental data, where an underestimated uncertainty interval is harder to catch than an inaccurate central estimate. Existing benchmarks evaluate scalar verbalized confidence on discrete question answering, subjective priors without data, or code execution for point predictions, leaving procedural propagation of experimental uncertainties untested. We introduce pullgym, an evaluation and reinforcement learning environment comprising 12 procedural physics experiment families across four difficulty tiers: clean Gaussian and Poisson statistics, background nuisance parameters, instrument systematics from calibration certificates, and low-count physical boundaries. Given simulated measurements and an apparatus logbook, an agent writes Python code to report five quantiles (2.5%, 16%, 50%, 84%, 97.5%) of the target quantity, which a separate sandbox scores against exact ground truth using a strictly proper clipped log-density rule without an LLM judge. Multi-turn frontier agents (deepseek-flash, kimi-k3.1-pro) reach 66.2%-70.4% empirical coverage at the nominal 68% level with unit sharpness on valid episodes, failing mainly by exhausting turn budgets on multi-parameter fits. By contrast, single-turn Qwen3-8B drops to 38.1% coverage. In controlled Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) experiments across 1,600 evaluated episodes, standard binary point-accuracy rewards leave 10x unit errors and unmodeled gain uncertainties intact while reaching 80% zero-variance rollout starvation. Optimizing the clipped log score achieves 100% in-distribution validity (-0.528 vs. -1.738 mean reward), maintains 1.00 clean-tier sharpness without global width inflation, and raises paired out-of-distribution 68% coverage from 23.5% to 35.3%. Code and benchmark tasks are available at https://github.com/kekeandzeyu/pullgym.

title: A Full-Form Lexicon for Arabic Dialects Supporting Arabic NLP and Speech Technology
abstract: Arabic dialects pose a distinctive challenge for lexical resources: they are acquired natively and used primarily in speech, while lacking a standard orthography. This paper presents DiaLEX, a family of large-scale full-form lexicons for six Arabic dialects (Egyptian, Hijazi, Emirati, Syrian, Lebanese, and Palestinian), comprising approximately 220 million entries, or an estimated 880 million if proclitics are enumerated. Unlike conventional dictionaries, DiaLEX exhaustively covers inflected, conjugated, cliticized, and negated wordforms, generated by a rule-based templatic framework validated by native-speaker linguists. Each entry carries a rich set of morphological, phonetic, and orthographic attributes. This paper (1)~examines DiaLEX's layered representation, which pairs a variant-rich Arabic-script layer with DARS, a primarily phonemic romanization tuned for speech technology; (2)~describes the generation methods, illustrated by Palestinian Arabic; and (3)~compares DiaLEX with existing dialectal resources, particularly MADAR/CODA. Applications to speech technology, machine translation, morphological analysis, and vocalization are discussed.

title: Mitigating representation bias through constrained optimization
abstract: Automated decision systems increasingly rely on people-related data, possibly amplifying discrimination already present in the real world. To prevent this, discrimination should be controlled throughout the data processing pipeline rather than assessed only on the final outcome. It may originate either from the data itself (representation bias) or from the algorithms that process the data (algorithmic bias), and can be characterized through properties such as coverage, which ensures sufficient representation of each protected group in the data, and fairness, which limits disparities among protected groups. This thesis focuses on data transformation, the preparation step in which a dataset is reshaped before analysis. This step deserves particular attention since it can amplify representation bias and propagate it to subsequent processing stages. This work investigates query rewriting as a way of correcting such bias. Given a selection query whose result violates a set of discrimination-aware constraints, the objective is to derive an alternative query that satisfies them while departing as little as possible from the original, thus preserving the analyst’s intent and the transparency of the transformation. Most existing query rewriting techniques address only one discrimination-related constraint at a time, enforcing either coverage or fairness over the query result, but not both simultaneously. To overcome this limitation, an initial optimization framework was proposed to jointly enforce coverage and fairness while minimizing deviation from the original query through a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) formulation. Its experimental evaluation, however, revealed scalability limitations, motivating the development of new optimization approaches. Building on this initial framework, this thesis first provides an extensive experimental investigation of the MINLP-based approach and then introduces a continuous reformulation of the query rewriting problem. The new model operates directly on the query selection constants, eliminating the discretized search space and enabling more scalable optimization techniques. The resulting problem is solved using a Differential Evolution-based approach. The two formulations are evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets and compared with state-of-the-art techniques under three settings: coverage constraints, fairness constraints, and their joint enforcement. The experimental results show a better trade-off among effectiveness, efficiency, and rewriting quality compared to the considered baseline approaches. Moreover, both formulations support the joint enforcement of coverage and fairness constraints, a setting not addressed by existing query rewriting techniques.

title: The concept of financial models for scaling artificial intelligence systems for development and security
abstract: Subject. The concept of financial models for scaling artificial intelligence (AI) systems in the context of development and security. Objectives. Suggest and justify new financial models for scaling AI systems that provide companies and organizations with safe development and effective investment in AI technologies. Methods. An interdisciplinary approach is applied, combining elements of risk management theory, AI economics, and security studies. Results. The challenges and risks associated with the process of scaling AI systems are detailed. The Comprehensive System for Secure Scaling of AI Systems is proposed and argued. The specific features of financial planning for the secure scaling of AI systems are substantiated. Based on existing financial mechanisms, alternative models of this process are proposed. Methods for evaluating the efficiency of investments in this process are identified and grouped by functional criterion. Conclusions and Relevance. The concept of financial models for the secure scaling of AI systems, as a comprehensive and multi-level approach, is essential for expanding the practical capabilities of AI and guaranteeing its security, ethics, and sustainability. The proposed security system encompasses risk management, continuous monitoring, and adaptation of advanced technologies. Evaluating the efficiency of investments in the secure scaling of AI systems goes beyond traditional financial metrics and therefore requires consideration of quantitative and qualitative aspects, economic benefits, innovation potential, competitiveness, pricing, and ethical factors. The results can be applied in managing resources and capital when scaling AI platforms, assessing related financial risks, ensuring security, as well as in developing regulatory frameworks and attracting investments.

title: When Imagination Lies: Frozen World Models Overrate the Policies They Train
abstract: A policy trained inside a learned world model is graded by the model it is optimized against. We measure what that does to the grade. Actor-critic agents train inside frozen TD-MPC2 models on three DeepMind Control tasks, and every checkpoint is scored in paired imagined and real episodes. We pre-registered a rise-then-fall curve for real return; it did not hold (the primary and two of three secondary hypotheses failed). The registered fallback did: the imagined-minus-real gap grows with training in every task (pooled exponent 0.268, 95% CI [0.238, 0.312]), from near zero to about 700–800 points on a 1,000-point scale at the smallest data size. In an exploratory exact-dynamics control, the same actor-critic, initialization, training starts, horizon, and bootstrapped critic, trained on true simulator transitions, does not collapse (late real return 615 versus 149), with either the simulator's or the learned reward, and the frozen model under-predicts these actors by 122 points while over-predicting its own by 731. This points to the policy exploiting the learned dynamics, not to critic bootstrapping or to reward error on real states. title: TDS-DP11: Daemonless Agent Context-Reduction Architecture Combining Six-Factor State-Sealed Summary Caching and Hash-Matched Zero-Byte Three-Tier Active Skill Loading
abstract: Large language model agents operating dozens of local tools and manuals repeatedly load multi-kilobyte skill documents and redundant query outputs into their context windows, incurring severe token overhead and context pollution. Existing server-side key-value or embedding-based semantic caches require resident GPU servers and frequently return stale or failed outputs after tool versions, runtime environments, or source files change. This defensive publication documents a daemonless agent context-reduction architecture bounded strictly by Korean Patent Application No. 10-2026-0238730 (filed November 25, 2026). The system combines a six-factor state-sealed summary cache that blocks confidential strings prior to storage (exit code 3), enforces a UTF-8 2,048-byte summary ceiling for COMMITTED records while physically isolating HOLD and FAILED outcomes into a separate quarantine directory (90_ROTATION_HOLD), and validates all six conditions via an append-only index (CACHE_INDEX.jsonl) with a hash-matched three-tier active skill loader that omits payload transmission (loaded_bytes = 0, content_omitted = True) whenever the caller's expected_sha256 matches the current skill file digest, returning only the requested tier (L0, L1, or L2) upon mismatch. Priority Patent Reference: Korean Patent Application No. 10-2026-0238730 (filed November 25, 2026). No Patent License Granted. Official Research Portal: https://tdskorea.com/

title: Keeping the What-If: A Record for Counterfactual World Models
abstract: This note is built around its findings. A record that holds the observed outcome lets an agent ask a what-if later, and the gain is measured in percent. One event: 82.6% improvement. Mean across 2000 events: 65.9% improvement. Chaining across two steps: 408% improvement in goals reached. From WILD to MATURE trust: 264% improvement. The rest of this note explains the record that produced those numbers, and the limits that still apply to them. A world model trained only on what did happen cannot answer what would have happened under a different action, whatever its data or capacity. Balestriero, LeCun, and Varaku solve the one-step version of that problem [1]. This note does not correct their paper. It asks a separate question: what does an agent need in order to ask that what-if later, after the step is over, for hindsight planning, debugging, and audit? The proposal here is a record as one way to hold the observed outcome for later use, not the only way, and not a way the paper itself needs. This is a supplement in reply to Balestriero, LeCun, and Varaku, arXiv:2611.24778.

title: A Likelihood Ratio Is Not a Whole Reading: What Class-Conditional Guard Models Change About Shortcuts, Calibration and Position, Why the Generative-Classifier Evidence Does Not Transfer to a Discriminatively Trained Ratio, and the Matched Comparison That Would Assign the Gains
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research Guard models screen the prompts sent to a language model and the responses it returns, and almost all of them are trained to emit one verdict token. A 2026 proposal argues that this objective is the root of three familiar failures - reliance on shortcut cues, overconfidence, and sensitivity to where the evidence sits in the input - and replaces it with a class-conditional score: a masked diffusion model reconstructs the moderated text under a "safe" and an "unsafe" hypothesis, and the difference of the two log-likelihoods is the verdict. Among thirteen guards on the authors' held-out benchmarks, the resulting guard posts the best average F1 and the lowest calibration error. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the measured gains are real but that the attribution to the objective is not yet earned. Four things change at once in that comparison: the training loss, the backbone and its attention mask, the training data and fine-tuning regime, and the inference compute. The loss that is actually optimised is a binary cross-entropy on the likelihood difference, which is a discriminative loss over a generative parameterisation; the argument that generative classifiers avoid shortcuts because they must model every feature was established for pure class-conditional training, and in the strongest text evidence for it adding an unconditional generative term to a discriminative loss did not help. The one same-backbone ablation reads a verdict from weights never trained to produce one, so it isolates a readout, not an objective. The generative-classifier record outside guards is two-sided, and the side favouring generative models is weakest for pretrained models fine-tuned on ample data, which is the guard setting. A documented refusal-cue shortcut sits in one of the two training sets, and nothing in a class-conditional model stops it from being learned. The paper consolidates the measured values in two tables and a figure, separates what each published number can and cannot support, and specifies a factorial audit - objective, backbone, data and readout varied one at a time, with threshold sweeps, post-hoc calibration and cue-insertion tests - stating which outcome would support which reading.

title: Optimal Consistent Guessing in Bulls and Cows
abstract: A simple Bulls and Cows solver always guesses the smallest remaining possible secret. What should it guess if it wants to finish in the fewest turns on average? We solve the decision tree under the rule that every guess must still be a possible secret. With four distinct decimal digits the optimal total is 26,688 guesses over 5,040 secrets when a leading zero is allowed, and 23,620 over 4,536 secrets when it is forbidden. An eleven-secret position shows why the guess leaving the fewest candidates on average can take longer to finish. In a 216-secret position, reuse of solved states, symmetry and lower bounds reduce the number of guess evaluations from 94,765,680 to 34,531 while selecting the same guess. We give exact averages through length four and bounds through length ten. In a separate four-digit experiment with no leading zero, allowing probes outside the remaining candidates yields a playable strategy costing 23,499 guesses.

title: MemoChain: Verifiable Constant-Size Memory for Language Models
abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents carry memory either as an ever-growing prompt (O(n) tokens per query) or as a vector store (O(n) index, no synthesis). We present MemoChain, a neural memory that is constant-size, streaming, and cryptographically verifiable. The entire history of a document collection or chat session folds into a fixed 22,528-byte state (11 heads x 32 keys x 32 values, Q14 fixed-point int16) updated by a Delta rule in O(1) per document. Because the fold is pure integer arithmetic, the same inputs produce bit-identical state digests in Python, native Rust, and a zkVM, which lets us attach Mina-style recursive zero-knowledge proofs: a third party verifies in ~28 ms that a 22 KB memory capsule was honestly computed from a committed input sequence under a committed writer, without re-reading the history and without seeing the raw inputs. We train the memory without any teacher model: gradients from a frozen causal LM's cross-entropy loss flow through differentiable memory-token injection, a reader head, and a straight-through Q14 quantizer into the Delta-rule writer. On held-out PersonaMem-style QA (4,237 questions, 30 unseen users, 200 documents each), the self-trained 22 KB capsule lifts a frozen Qwen3-8B decoder from 58.18% to 64.69% (hard questions 30.84% to 38.16%), matching a 388 MB cross-attention memory teacher (64.76% / 38.16%) whose KV cache occupies 4.10 MB, at 181.8x smaller memory and with zero teacher dependence in training. A capacity ablation shows the memory gain saturates at a 10 KiB state on gist-style QA: growing the state 8.8x moves the gain by only +0.007 nats. Training the same 22 KB capsule on a real developer's 241 coding sessions doubles coding-session recall (+0.94 to +1.76 nats) while retaining 96.6% of the personal-QA gain. We release the full stack: an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible memory proxy in daily use (~55 MB RAM, 0 extra GPU, 90% measured input-token reduction on local vLLM and 66.8% billed cost reduction on OpenRouter), bit-exact Rust and SP1 zkVM implementations, and an honesty audit including negative results.

title: THE LAW OF MULTIFLOW GENERATIVE IMPACT VELOCITY 10.5281/zenodo.24545422
authors: Principal Inventor & Author: Prof. Dr. Abdulghani Ali Mansour Abdulhamid Chief Cybernetic Architect & Sustainability Researcher El-Spei
abstract: The invention concerns a multi-level regenerative cybernetic law for representing, evaluating, controlling and verifying the evolution of generative impact across multiple interacting flows and system domains. The law is designed to preserve non-substitution among critical dimensions, compute generative impact velocities, evaluate multi-flow interactions, project future system trajectories, trigger autonomous intervention under defined adverse conditions, and preserve execution evidence through an immutable validation ledger. The law is situated within the I-RSTIG architecture and is intended to be executable through a multi-component kernel such as UGRCK. The Generative Impact Velocity Engine (GIVE) performs the impact-velocity computation assigned to it; it is one engine within the wider kernel and is not equated with the kernel as a whole. Other kernel components may ingest and normalize telemetry, validate non-substitution constraints, consolidate multi-flow information, project trajectories, intercept unsafe execution, and record cryptographic evidence. The specification defines a baseline single-system law and a proposed multi-flow extension, then describes networked and nested-level operation, control invariants, execution interfaces, verification requirements and a preliminary claim set. The foundational objective is Generative Transgenerational Holistic Impact.
